facts.fact: The Namibia Statistics Agency states that the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security registers births and deaths and issues the certificates, on the National Population Registration System, whose data the agency obtains from the Office of the Prime Minister, which manages it; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The Namibia Statistics Agency states that a five-year CRVS National Strategic Plan for 2015/16 to 2020/21 was approved by Cabinet in 2015, following the 2014 comprehensive assessment, with national steering and technical committees set up to implement it; the report names no later plan.

The Namibia Statistics Agency reports births and deaths registered and captured on the NPRS in 2018 to 2021 (85,853 births and 24,388 deaths registered in 2021, from records captured up to 17 February 2022); marriages are captured on it at head office only, since 2014.

The Namibia Statistics Agency states that applications are processed and captured onto the NPRS and certificates issued by the local civil registration office, with registration at national, regional and sub-regional level and at most district hospitals and the information available in real time across the 14 regions; capture is delayed at some remote offices lacking computers or internet, and paper records are still couriered to head office for archiving. No date is given, so the published date is used.

The Namibia Statistics Agency reports that the share of registered births captured on the NPRS within 14 days fell from 87.1 per cent in 2018 to 68.9 per cent in 2021, while deaths captured within 14 days rose from 58.0 to 89.6 per cent; 96.2 per cent of births and 92.5 per cent of deaths were captured within 12 months in 2021.

The Namibia Statistics Agency states that some registration offices in remote areas lack computers or internet connectivity, so that capture of records on the NPRS may be delayed; it gives no count of offices, with or without the system. No date is given, so the published date is used.

facts.fact: A UNICEF and UN Legal Identity Agenda case study states that the Department of Civil Registration of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security manages the system, which stores births, adoptions, marriages, divorces and deaths in the NPRS, with the Prime Minister's Office leading and coordinating; no date is given, so the published date is used.
The case study states that the digital facilities were developed within the country with its own resources; it gives no budget figure and no date, so the published date is used.

The case study states that a CRVS Strategic Plan was formulated in 2014-15 and approved by Cabinet, and that the national CRVS Technical Committee set up to implement it, chaired by the Ministry of Home Affairs, remains in place; it names no later plan.
The case study's milestones give the NPRS as established in 2011, its death registration module deployed in 2012 and its birth registration module in 2013, with the marriage module following in 2014.

The case study states that births and deaths are registered electronically in real time in the NPRS at local registration centres, while marriages are entered in it at head office only and customary marriages and divorces are not recorded; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The case study states that all local registration centres are connected to the NPRS, enabling real-time electronic registration of births and deaths into it, and that birth and death certificates are issued locally and on the spot from the NPRS; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The case study states that birth and death registration takes place in 62 local registration centres (it lists 14 regional offices, 24 Category I and 21 Category II sub-regional offices, which sum to 59), with 24 health facilities and hospitals also registering, and that all the local registration centres are connected to the NPRS; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The same case study lists among its challenges that the lack of connectivity to the NPRS in certain sub-regional offices continues to hinder timely capture of records and verification for duplicate documents, with no count of those offices; no date is given, so the published date is used.

slug: 2021-01-01 Building Resilient CRVS Systems amid COVID-19 - Namibia (Technical Brief)

facts.fact: The brief (Bayer Forsingdal and Munyika, for the Centre of Excellence for CRVS Systems, APAI-CRVS and ECA) states that four years after the 2010 launch of the digitisation project the online, integrated electronic NPRS was fully functional and installed in 95 per cent of civil registration offices; it gives no count of offices.

The brief reports 64,283 birth records entered in the electronic birth register of the NPRS in January to August 2020 (92,616 in the same months of 2019, 77,224 in 2018; all ages, with amendments and some duplicates) and, from NPRS operational statistics, 14,033 deaths registered in January to August 2020.

The brief describes registration at the civil registration office: the registrar validates the application, pulls the e-notification data into the online NPRS, captures the remaining data and at once issues an electronically printed certificate, in under five minutes; the process is undated and is dated here to the brief's 2020 study period.

The brief states that the digitisation project that produced the electronic NPRS was launched in 2010 and led jointly by the Office of the Prime Minister and the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security, and was completed in 2014.

The brief states that after the state of emergency of 17 March 2020 a total of 22 birth and death registration offices at health facilities were temporarily closed, only regional and sub-regional offices stayed open, and late registration and duplicate certificates were suspended; most services were restored by September 2020.

facts.fact: The Centre of Excellence for CRVS Systems case study states that the Department of Civil Registration of the Ministry of Home Affairs and Immigration registers births and deaths through its regional directorate, and that the Office of the Prime Minister develops and maintains the NPRS; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The case study states that from 2000 the Office of the Prime Minister, with the ministry, designed and built the NPRS locally using internal resources, and calls it a homegrown register built with internal resources; it gives no budget figure, and the published date is used.

The case study states that a five-year civil registration and vital statistics strategic plan was drafted in 2014 by the ministry with the Namibia Statistics Agency, and that the e-Government Strategic Action Plan 2014 to 2018, led by the Office of the Prime Minister, treats an interoperable NPRS as a key part of the e-government vision.
The case study's timeline gives the birth registration module of the NPRS as designed and piloted in the Khomas Region in 2011.

The case study's timeline gives the death module of the NPRS as designed and deployed in 2012 and the birth registration module as deployed nationwide in 2013, with the marriage module in 2014; the civil registration system was built on the identity platform step by step from 2010 to 2014.

The case study states that the workstations used to enter registered information electronically are permanently linked with the NPRS, allowing real-time data communication and electronic validation, and that registration is completed at a ministry office, including the birth registration office at the health facility; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The case study states that the ministry has a network of 55 offices across the country (14 regional offices, 23 hospital-based facilities and 18 sub-regional offices, 9 of which enrol for identity documents) and still works with a few magistrate courts on birth and death registration; it gives no separate count of offices entering records in the NPRS, and the published date is used.
